questions.prompt: Which lifecycle hook runs once the component's DOM exists, making it the right place for initial data fetching or DOM access?
questions.explanation: onMounted runs after the component is inserted into the DOM, so template refs are available and it's a natural place to fetch initial data.

questions.prompt: How does watchEffect differ from watch?

options.text: watchEffect runs only on the server
watchEffect runs immediately and auto-tracks reactive state it reads; watch is lazy with explicit sources

questions.explanation: watchEffect runs its function right away and re-runs when any reactive value it read changes. watch is lazy, takes explicit sources, and provides old and new values.

questions.prompt: Where should you clean up a timer or event listener that you set up in onMounted?

options.text: You don't need to clean it up

questions.explanation: Pair setup with cleanup: tear down timers, listeners, and subscriptions in onUnmounted so they don't leak after the component is removed.

questions.prompt: By default, a watcher callback runs BEFORE the DOM updates. To run it AFTER the DOM updates, set flush to '______'. (one word)
questions.explanation: The default flush is 'pre' (before DOM update). Use flush: 'post' when the callback needs to read the updated DOM.

questions.prompt: Why must lifecycle hooks be called synchronously inside setup (not inside an if or after await)?

options.text: So Vue can associate them with the current component instance; otherwise they may fail to register

questions.explanation: Hooks register callbacks against the active component instance during setup. Calling them conditionally or after an await can break that association.

questions.prompt: Match each tool to its typical job.

pairs.right: Fetch data / access the DOM after mount
React to a specific source with old + new values
Keep something in sync with the state it reads

questions.explanation: onMounted/onUnmounted bracket setup and cleanup; watch reacts to an explicit source; watchEffect auto-tracks whatever it reads.
